roadmaps.title: Beejs Networking Essentials
roadmaps.summary: The Beejs Networking Essentials path, from the LockDrop Knowledge Base.

steps.title: Networking Overview, Sockets API, Layered Models & HTTP Client/Server
steps.summary: Foundational networking concepts, sockets lifecycle, protocol layering (Internet & OSI models), and building a basic HTTP client and server in Python.

steps.title: IP Addressing, Subnets, Web Server & Packet Framing
steps.summary: IPv4 and IPv6 addressing and subnets, building a file-serving HTTP server, byte ordering/endianness, stream packet framing, and the Atomic Time and Word Server projects.

steps.title: Transport Protocols (TCP & UDP) & TCP Checksum Validation
steps.summary: TCP reliability, handshakes, flow and congestion control; UDP datagrams and fragmentation; and implementing TCP checksum validation with the IP pseudo-header.

steps.title: Subnet Math, IP Routing, Link Layer, ARP & Graph Pathfinding
steps.summary: Bitwise IPv4 subnetting and netfuncs project, IP routing and TTL, Ethernet frames and CSMA/CD vs CSMA/CA, ARP and Wireshark capture, Dijkstra routing simulation, and Packet Tracer labs.

steps.title: Beej's Guide to Network Programming — Install the software.
steps.summary: Packet Tracer switch and router labs, select() I/O multiplexing, DNS hierarchy and dig project, NAT and DHCP, port scanning and firewalls, input security, multiuser chat project, and bitwise/threading/JSON appendices.

roadmaps.title: Linux Essentials
roadmaps.summary: The Linux Essentials path, from the LockDrop Knowledge Base.

steps.title: Linux Origins and the Open Source Application Landscape
steps.summary: Trace Linux from a 1991 kernel project to the distributions powering phones, desktops and servers — and learn to choose between Debian, Ubuntu and RHEL without guessing.

steps.title: Open Source Licensing, ICT Skills and Working in Linux
steps.summary: Cut through GPL, BSD and Creative Commons: know which licences let you ship proprietary code, which force you to publish, and how open-source businesses actually make money.

steps.title: Command Line Basics and Getting Help
steps.summary: Work fluently in the shell: compose commands with pipes and quotes, control variables and PATH, and find any answer with man, info, locate and find.

steps.title: Directories, Listing Files and Creating, Moving and Deleting Files
steps.summary: Navigate the filesystem hierarchy like a native, master ls flags, and create, move, copy and delete files with confidence — including hidden and permission-sensitive cases.

steps.title: Archiving Files and Searching and Extracting Data
steps.summary: Compress and archive with gzip, bzip2, xz and tar, redirect streams exactly where you want them, and slice text with head, tail, grep and friends.

steps.title: Turning Commands into Scripts and Choosing an Operating System
steps.summary: Turn repeated commands into real shell scripts with variables, arguments, conditionals and exit codes — then pick a distro based on lifecycle, not fashion.

steps.title: Understanding Computer Hardware and Where Data Is Stored
steps.summary: Read a machine from the board up: CPU, RAM, UEFI, disks, RAID, partitions and the /dev and /sys trees that expose them to Linux.

steps.title: Your Computer on the Network and Basic Security
steps.summary: Follow a packet from MAC address to DNS lookup: IPv4 and IPv6, CIDR, routing, resolv.conf and the account model that keeps a system safe.

steps.title: Creating Users and Groups, and Managing Permissions and Ownership
steps.summary: Create users and groups, decode /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, and control access with chmod, ownership and special bits — including what only root can do.

steps.title: Special Directories and Files
steps.summary: Understand /tmp, /run and sticky bits, count hard links, and tell a symlink from a real file — the small filesystem details that cause big surprises.
